options: A synonym for T-SQL running against a KQL Database
A configuration language for Eventstreams only
A subset of PySpark's DataFrame API
A real, purpose-built query language for a KQL Database — genuinely its own language, not a dialect of T-SQL
questions.explain: Both KQL and T-SQL are declarative query languages, but KQL is genuinely its own language.

questions.q: What does the pipe operator (|) do in a KQL query?
options: It replaces the need for a table name entirely
It's purely decorative and has no functional effect
It only works with the where operator, no others
Chains a sequence of operators, each transforming the result of the operator before it, in the literal order written
questions.explain: This is genuinely closer to a PySpark method chain (.filter().select()) than to T-SQL's clause structure.

questions.q: What is the real, substantive difference between KQL's pipe order and T-SQL's clause order?
options: T-SQL's clauses have a fixed logical evaluation order regardless of typed order; KQL's pipe steps execute in the exact literal order written
KQL has no concept of order at all
T-SQL clauses execute in the order they're typed, just like KQL
There's no real difference between the two
questions.explain: This becomes especially relevant once summarize (Lesson 24) and joins (Lesson 25) enter the picture.

questions.q: Why does this course teach KQL as its own language rather than "SQL with different keywords"?
options: This course never actually compares KQL to T-SQL
Treating it that way causes real confusion the moment pipe-order semantics matter, in a way T-SQL's clause-based structure never requires thinking about
KQL and T-SQL are actually identical, so the distinction doesn't matter
KQL cannot express any filtering logic at all
questions.explain: The chapter draws T-SQL and PySpark parallels only where they genuinely hold, not as a blanket equivalence.

questions.q: Which KQL operator corresponds to T-SQL's WHERE clause?
options: | take
| project
| summarize
| where
questions.explain: project corresponds to SELECT's column choice, and take corresponds to TOP.
